coupling: The clipping commit changes the right-surface bound from an inclusive col_max to an exclusive col_limit and adds cell_add_visible(), an unchecked helper used only where that commit’s loop arithmetic proves the column is visible; its endpoint remains checked, so a one-past endpoint is harmless there. The later wide-accumulator commit templates that helper for 64-bit rows and consumes col_limit as an inclusive endpoint bound (cx1 <= col_limit) only when more than 255 edges select the wide path. The overflow therefore requires the later unchecked wide endpoint together with the earlier exclusive-bound/helper contract: the first commit has no wide consumer, while the second commit’s local change looks like a bounds-checked optimization unless the boundary semantics introduced by the first commit are traced across commits. A correct repair must reconcile the cross-commit boundary contract with the unchecked helper rather than reasoning about either diff in isolation.
